factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.90–0.97) of Token split, Number of empty sequence flows, Control flow complexity, Size and Coefficient of network connectivity mark a factor of net size together with the amount of splitting and parallel structure that grows with it. Maximum connector degree (0.76, also 0.39 on Factor 2) and Connector Mismatch (0.55, communality 0.35) join more moderately, and Density loads negatively (-0.46), consistent with larger nets being sparser.

factors.name: Connector density and fan-out
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89) and Density (0.84) load positively, while Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.58), so nets high on this factor have dense, high-degree connectors that tend to be of one type. Density also has a secondary negative loading on Factor 1 (-0.46), and Connector Heterogeneity has a low communality (0.35), so the factor rests mainly on two measures.

factors.name: Sequential structuredness
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.96) and Separability (0.69) define this factor, capturing how much of the net consists of plain sequential arcs and cut-vertex-separated parts rather than connector-rich regions. It rests on only two measures, and the Sequentiality loading is affected by a possible Heywood case (communality 1.017).

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83, so the data are suitable for factor analysis; three varimax factors explain 82% of the variance. Factor 1 (49%) is a dominant size/branching factor, Factor 2 (17%) reflects connector degree and density, and Factor 3 (16%) reflects sequentiality and separability. No cross-loadings above the gap rule were flagged and no measure is unassigned, though Maximum connector degree, Density and Coefficient of network connectivity show notable secondary loadings.
caveats: Sequentiality has a communality above 1 (possible Heywood case), so its loading and Factor 3 should be read with caution.
Factors 2 and 3 rest on only two or three measures each, making them less robust than Factor 1.
Connector Mismatch and Connector Heterogeneity have low communalities (about 0.35), so they are poorly represented by the solution.
Number of duplicate tasks was removed as constant, so the analysis says nothing about label duplication.
The structure reflects shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depends on the discovery algorithms, the varimax rotation and the choice of three factors.
